title: Securing a Three-Tier Architecture on AWS – The Right Way | Mahesh Divakaran Nair
content: Mahesh Divakaran Nair 10mo Report this post Securing a Three-Tier Architecture on AWS – The Right Way In cloud architecture, security is not an afterthought — it’s baked into every layer. Design of a secure Three-Tier Architecture in AWS, with each layer protected using AWS-native security services: Presentation Layer (Web/App Frontend) AWS WAF – Block malicious traffic Amazon CloudFront – Global content delivery + DDoS protection (via AWS Shield) AWS Certificate Manager – SSL/TLS for secure communication Application Layer (App Servers / Logic) Security Groups – Strict inbound/outbound rules AWS Systems Manager – Patch management & secure access without SSH keys IAM Roles – Least-privilege access to backend services Data Layer (Database / Storage) Amazon RDS Security – Encryption at rest (KMS) + in transit Private Subnet Placement – No public internet exposure AWS Backup – Automated & encrypted backups Network Security VPC with Public & Private Subnets – Isolate tiers NACLs – Extra layer of subnet-level filtering VPC Flow Logs – Traffic visibility for anomaly detection Included centralized logging & monitoring via Amazon CloudWatch and AWS GuardDuty for threat detection. Every request flows through multiple layers of AWS security services before touching your data ( #DefenceinDepth ). This layered approach drastically reduces the attack surface and ensures compliance-readiness. 62 12 Comments Like Comment Share Copy LinkedIn Facebook X Kevin C. 10mo Report this comment Those resources within the application layer are not application layer at all. The application layer consists of EC2, Lambda functions, ECS/EKS, and containers running application code. What you described is more like a management plane and not an application layer at all.
